headline: Rates, oil and the dollar are all speeding up at once, and only AI stocks are holding the index up.
summary: The S&P 500 is flat for the month, but that hides a lot. The equal-weight index has lagged the cap-weighted one by 5% in a month, which is a 2.5-sigma move. Transports are down 9% against the S&P, and banks, homebuilders, retailers and utilities all fell 5–9%. A handful of AI names (semis, META, AMD, MU) are carrying the tape.

Behind it is a triple squeeze that is accelerating. The 2-year yield is up 70bp in a month and the 10-year is at 5.18%, the highest since 2007. Real yields are up 53bp while breakevens are flat, so this is a real tightening, not an inflation scare. Brent is up 20% to $107 on the Hormuz blockade. The dollar has turned up. Bond volatility (MOVE) is up 45%, while the VIX sits at 16. The Fed hiked to 3.75–4% and says another hike is coming.

Druckenmiller's own words this month: rates are "at best too low", and the AI build-out is "late stage". He has cut his AI exposure to a fifth of what it was six months ago. The playbook: short what rates and oil hurt (housing, the consumer, transports), own energy, fade parabolic semis against software, and buy cheap equity protection while the VIX ignores the bond market.

good.text: Copper is at a record while gold falls. Copper/gold is up 10% in a month, so the economy is running hot, not rolling over. That is also why yields can keep rising.
Credit is calm for now. Junk bonds are outperforming Treasuries and leveraged loans are in an uptrend, so no default wave is being priced.
Core inflation is 2.4% and breakevens are flat at 2.33%. The oil shock has not spread into core prices yet.
Energy leads, with earnings to match: XLE is up 43% this year and 11% ahead of the S&P over 3 months.
Crypto is on the come. Bitcoin is up 41% in 3 months and back above its 200-day, with ETH and SOL following. This is usually an early liquidity tell.

bad.text: Yields are speeding up, and the front end leads. The 2-year is up 70bp in a month and the 10-year is at 5.18%. Real yields are up 53bp. That is what compresses multiples.
The oil shock is accelerating: Brent is up 20% in a month and gasoline has nearly doubled this year. It works as a tax on the consumer and feeds the Fed's reason to hike.
Breadth is collapsing under a flat index. Equal-weight lost 5% and small caps 6% against the S&P in one month. Transports are failing to confirm (Dow theory).
Housing is cracking. Mortgage rates are 7.03%, the fifth straight weekly rise, and homebuilders are down 20% against the S&P in 3 months. Home Depot is down 13% in a month.
Financials and private credit are rolling over: Blackstone is down 18% and Goldman 12% in a month, and regional banks are losing ground.
The dollar has turned up and is accelerating. That tightens global conditions and has just knocked gold down 8%.

trades.name: Homebuilders
trades.expr: Short ITB (or XHB). Hedge-fund version: short ITB / long SPY.
trades.thesis: The cleanest way to monetize the rates move. Mortgages are above 7%, builders are already cutting prices, and the group is in a relative downtrend with no bottom yet.
trades.trigger: 10y at 5.18% and still rising; ITB −9% in a month, −18% vs S&P over 3 months.
trades.stop: The 10y closes back below 4.75%, or ITB regains its 200-day.
trades.line: Short ITB: mortgages above 7% and rising

trades.name: Oil tax on the consumer
trades.expr: Long XLE / short XLY, equal dollars
trades.thesis: Brent at $107 and accelerating takes money from households and hands it to producers. Energy is the only sector with rising relative strength, while discretionary is in a relative downtrend. The pair profits if oil stays high even when the market falls.
trades.trigger: Brent +20% in a month; XLE rel. strength +11% (3m); XLY/XLP in a downtrend.
trades.stop: A Hormuz deal that sends Brent back below $90. This is the gap risk, so size for it.
trades.line: Long XLE / short XLY: $107 Brent taxes the shopper

trades.name: Long bonds
trades.expr: Short TLT, or pay 10y/30y swaps. Alternatively sell 2y futures to express the Fed.
trades.thesis: Druckenmiller says policy is still too easy and the Fed is now hiking into a weak-auction, big-deficit backdrop. The 2-year has moved most, so the market is still catching up to the Fed.
trades.trigger: 2y +70bp in a month and accelerating; MOVE +45%; TLT in a downtrend.
trades.stop: The 10y back below 4.85%. If equities crack hard, bonds rally as a haven, so take profits into any equity panic.
trades.line: Short TLT: the Fed is hiking and the 2-year leads

trades.name: Fade parabolic semis, own software
trades.expr: Long IGV / short SOXX (or trim MU, AMD)
trades.thesis: Druckenmiller has cut AI to 20% of its peak and calls the build-out late stage. MU is 64% and AMD 73% above their 200-day averages, and semis are up 88% this year. Software has already been de-rated and is now turning up in relative strength.
trades.trigger: SOXX +26% above its 200-day; IGV rel. strength +21% (3m) and turning up.
trades.stop: SOXX makes new highs while breadth (RSP/SPY) turns up too.
trades.line: Long IGV / short SOXX: AI build-out is late stage

trades.name: Cheap crash protection
trades.expr: Buy 2–3 month SPY puts ~5% OTM, or a put spread; alternatively short IYT vs SPY
trades.thesis: Bond volatility is spiking but equity volatility is not. The VIX at 16 prices none of the rates, oil or breadth stress. When transports and equal-weight break first, the index usually follows.
trades.trigger: MOVE 105 (+45% 1m) vs VIX 16; transports −10% vs S&P in a month.
trades.stop: It is a premium spend: budget it and let it expire if the VIX stays pinned.
trades.target: 3–5x on the premium in a 10% drawdown
trades.line: Buy SPY puts: VIX 16 while bond vol spikes

trades.name: Copper miners on the dip
trades.expr: Buy COPX or FCX on weakness, scaling in
trades.thesis: Copper just set a record, but the miners fell 10% with the market. Miners lagging the metal is a gap that usually closes. Electrification and a hot economy back the metal.
trades.trigger: Copper at a record, $6.77/lb; COPX −10% 1m but still above its 200-day.
trades.stop: COPX closes below its 200-day, or copper loses $6.
trades.line: Buy COPX: the metal is at a record, the miners are not
